confirmed.location: Discussion > Strengths and Limitations, second limitations paragraph (paragraph index 124), the sentence on study design

Every performance figure in the paper is agreement with PHQ-9 >= 10, an imperfect proxy whose own sensitivity and specificity against a semi-structured interview are roughly 0.85/0.85. For a depression-screening algorithm paper this is the first limitation a JMIR reviewer raises, and its absence reads as unawareness rather than as a settled choice.

verdicts.verdict: The manuscript is in submittable shape and holds up to an editorial read; one blocking fix and one substantive addition are needed, plus four copyedit-grade items. What is sound: every number in the Abstract reappears in Results at the identical value, and every one I could trace matches the authoritative six-digit CSVs after a single rounding (internal 0.836454, pre 0.765028, post 0.770591, delta 0.005563 with CI -0.044569 to 0.056146 and P=.8628; Table 2's full metric grid; all 12 NHANES race subgroup AUROCs and CIs and all 14 KCHS subgroup values; all four fairness flags at -0.056, -0.072, -0.078 and +0.074; the whole 17-step parsimony trajectory including the 0.0002-below and 0.0044-above margin arithmetic; all nine sensitivity rows; the operating point, net benefit, flag rates, SHAP values and Spearman rho; the oracle range 0.764-0.776 with CI 0.753-0.799 widening to 0.745-0.794, which matches review4_oracle_grouped.csv rather than the superseded oracle_ci.csv). All five aims are answered under their own headings, all four hypothesis verdicts are stated and justified (H1 met, H2 and H3 supported with the qualitative-margin caveat conceded in Limitations, H4 supported), the Conclusions claim no more than 0.765 and 0.771 support and hedge the six-item deployment claim as "plausible", references are numbered strictly in order of first citation with all 45 cited, figures are cited in order and captions 2 through 7 accurately describe their panels, and the prose is clean against every style rule tested: no banned pronouns (all "us" hits are the country), no "because", no result-clause "so" (only purpose-clause "so that"), no em dash, en dash, Unicode minus or smart quotes, correct "ie," form, and no P value with a leading zero. The one thing that must not go out as is: the Methods statistics paragraph contains a duplicated sentence, which is the sort of blemish that colors an editor's whole read. Second, the Limitations should concede that PHQ-9 >= 10 is a screening threshold and not a diagnostic reference standard, since that is the objection a JMIR reviewer will raise first and it is currently absent from both the manuscript and Appendix 1. Fix those two and the four minors, and it is ready.

The science is sound and the numbers are clean: I reconciled every value in Tables S1 and S3-S15 against the primary2_*.csv results (plus harmonization_sensitivity.csv, methods_explore.csv, review4_oracle_grouped.csv, ceiling_experiments.csv and deeplearning_explore.csv for the exploration tables) and found no discrepancy, no rounding drift, and no contradiction between the appendices and the manuscript. Tables S1 to S16 are present, gapless, each captioned, and each cited from the main text; every section name a pointer uses exists. One item must be fixed before submission: the Methods paragraph on performance summary prints the same sentence twice, verbatim in substance, which is the kind of thing a JMIR copyeditor bounces immediately. Beyond that, the defects are concentrated in the two appendices and are all mechanical: Multimedia Appendix 1 refers the reader to Multimedia Appendix 1 in ten places, six of its tables repeat every abbreviation twice in their footnotes, and two abbreviations (NB, PSI) are never expanded; Multimedia Appendix 2 has one row whose location claim outruns the manuscript (12c, on the tie-break and the "identical" grids) and one whose cited flow counts are appendix-only (20a).
